label: Bible Study
prompt: For this is the _____ that ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another.
verse: For this is the message that ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another.
note: The oldest message in the church — love one another, heard from the beginning.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he shall _____ you up.
verse: Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he shall lift you up.
note: Bow low before the Lord, James says, and He'll do the lifting.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And he divided the three hundred men into three companies, and he put a trumpet in every man's hand, with empty pitchers, and _____ within the pitchers.
verse: And he divided the three hundred men into three companies, and he put a trumpet in every man's hand, with empty pitchers, and lamps within the pitchers.
note: Three hundred men, each with a trumpet and a lamp hidden in an empty pitcher — Gideon's whole battle plan.

label: Deep Water
prompt: And he said, Who art thou? And she answered, I am Ruth thine handmaid: spread therefore thy _____ over thine handmaid; for thou art a near kinsman.
verse: And he said, Who art thou? And she answered, I am Ruth thine handmaid: spread therefore thy skirt over thine handmaid; for thou art a near kinsman.
note: Ruth's bold marriage request at the threshingfloor — the Hebrew for 'skirt' is the same as the 'wings' of Ruth 2:12.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: His glory is like the firstling of his bullock, and his horns are like the horns of _____: with them he shall push the people together to the ends of the earth: and they are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and they are the thousands of Manasseh.
verse: His glory is like the firstling of his bullock, and his horns are like the horns of unicorns: with them he shall push the people together to the ends of the earth: and they are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and they are the thousands of Manasseh.
note: Yes, the KJV has 'unicorns' — Moses' blessing on Joseph's mighty horns. Most modern versions say 'wild ox.'
